07.1Chapter 7 · Trust No One

Why Be So Paranoid?

LLM par bharosa karna aasan lagta hai kyunki woh confident aur fluent jawab deta hai — lekin yehi confidence sabse bada dhokha hai. Pehle chapters ke threats ko dobara dekho to samajh aayega ki paranoia yahan insanity nahi, necessity hai.

Prompt injection — model ka behaviour hijack

  • Direct prompt injection: attacker carefully crafted input se model ka behaviour badal deta hai — model woh karne lagta hai jo attacker chahta hai, developer ne jo socha tha woh nahi.
  • Indirect prompt injection: isme user seedha harmful input nahi deta — harmful content kisi aur jagah se aata hai, jaise web page, document ya email se, aur model use instruction samajh kar follow kar leta hai.
  • Chain attack ka khatra: prompt injection akela bhi khatarnak hai, lekin jab woh excessive agency jaisi kamzori se jud jaye to damage kai guna badh jata hai.

Sensitive information disclosure — model bahut kuch jaanta hai

  • Training data se leak: model apni training se seekhi hui confidential ya sensitive info — jaise password ya personal details — bina soche output mein de sakta hai.
  • OWASP Top 10 mein listed: ye risk itna serious hai ki OWASP ne ise apne LLM Top 10 mein jagah di hai — matlab ye edge case nahi, mainstream threat hai.
  • Discretion ki kami: model ko nahi pata ki kya bolna hai aur kya chhupana hai — woh sirf pattern follow karta hai, judgment nahi lagata.

Hallucination aur overreliance — psychological vulnerabilities

  • Hallucination: model confident tareeke se galat info bana leta hai — aisi baatein jo sach lagti hain lekin hain nahi. User ko pata bhi nahi chalta ki jawab fabricated hai.
  • Overreliance: user model ke output par andha bharosa karne lagta hai, bina verify kiye use sach maan leta hai — aur galti aage badh jati hai.
  • Dono ek saath khatarnak: model galat bole aur user bina check kiye maan le — ye combination decision-making ko barbaad kar sakta hai.

Toxic output — chatbot ki badtameezi

  • Pehle ke chatbots se sabak: pehle ke mashhoor chatbots toxic aur offensive output dene lage the — ye problem ek baar ki nahi, persistent hai.
  • Good judgment ki kami: tum apne chatbot par bharosa nahi kar sakte ki woh hamesha tameez se aur socially acceptable tareeke se jawab dega.
  • Reputation ka risk: ek toxic output user ko hurt bhi kar sakta hai aur tumhari service ki reputation ko bhi damage kar sakta hai.
Yaad rakho: In threats ko samajhna hi comprehensive security strategy ka pehla step hai — jab tak tum ye maan kar nahi chaloge ki model galti kar sakta hai, tum usko protect karne ka system bana hi nahi sakte.
SOURCESource: The Developer's Playbook for Large Language Model Security, O'Reilly, Chapter 7 — Trust No One
← Previous07 · Zero Trust Decoded→ Next07.2 · Zero Trust Architecture Implement Karo
07.2Chapter 7 · Trust No One

Zero Trust Architecture Implement Karo

Zero trust architecture LLM ke liye do complementary strategies par khada hai — pehle design stage par model ki unsupervised agency ko limit karo, aur dusra output ko aggressively filter karo. Ek ke bina dusra adhoora hai.

Do strategies — ek saath kaam karti hain

  • 1. Agency ko limit karo (design stage): model ko kya karne ki permission hai, ye design time par hi decide karo — baad mein patch karna mushkil aur risky hota hai.
  • 2. Output ko aggressively filter karo (safety net): design kitna bhi achha ho, kuch na kuch slip ho hi sakta hai — output filtering woh safety net hai jo harmful output ko user tak pahunchne se pehle pakad leta hai.
  • Dono ka balance: sirf design par bharosa karna na-kaafi hai, aur sirf filtering par bharosa karna bhi — dono milkar ek well-defined, well-guarded boundary banate hain.

Excessive agency — teen roop

  • Excessive permissions: LLM ko ek aur system user samjho — use sirf minimum required permissions do. Example: medical app mein RAG ke liye database ka READ access kaafi tha, lekin team ne LLM ko UPDATE, INSERT aur DELETE bhi de diye — phir ek malicious insider ne model ko trick karke patient records modify karwa diye aur billing info delete karwa di. Fix: wapas READ-only karo aur poora audit karo ki kuch manipulate to nahi hua.
  • Excessive autonomy: model ko direct action lene ki permission dena risky hai. Example: financial app pehle sirf portfolio analysis deta tha, phir team ne auto-rebalance feature add kar diya — attacker indirect prompt injection se model ko trick karke customer accounts se millions ke securities khareed-bikwa sakta hai. Fix: human in the loop — har trade se pehle customer review aur approve kare, thoda slow lekin bahut safe.
  • Excessive functionality: har naya feature achha nahi hota. Example: resume screening app ko expand karke LLM se candidate recommend karwana shuru kar diya — ye European Union ke naye hiring rules ke against nikla aur company par millions ka fine laga. Fix: regulatory environment samjho, compliance aur risk team ke saath kaam karo, aisi functionality mat do jo rules tode.

Confused deputy problem

  • Kya hai ye: deputy (LLM) ke paas client se zyada privileges hote hain, aur attacker deputy ko manipulate karke uske privileges ka misuse karwata hai — fayda attacker ko, nuksaan tumhe.
  • Purana attack, naya scale: ye attack type pehle se known hai, lekin LLM ke zamane mein ye bahut zyada common hone wala hai kyunki LLM aksar high-privilege actions kar sakta hai.
  • Bachav: least privilege + human approval — deputy ke paas zyada power hi mat rakho, aur critical action se pehle human check mandatory rakho.

Securing output handling — OWASP ka #2 risk

  • Insecure output handling: OWASP Top 10 for LLM apps mein ye dusra sabse bada risk vote hua — matlab output ki validation, sanitization aur management mein kami ek top-level vulnerability hai.
  • Toxic output: bina check ke model socially unacceptable ya inappropriate content de sakta hai.
  • PII disclosure: bina filtering ke model sensitive personal info leak kar sakta hai — privacy aur legal dono ka risk.
  • Rogue code execution: model ka code output agar system ke dusre hisse mein execute ho jaye to SQL injection aur XSS jaise attacks ho sakte hain — model ka code kabhi blindly execute mat karo.
Yaad rakho: LLM ko safety-critical ya financial decision bina human oversight ke kabhi mat lene do — aaj ki technology mein misinterpretation aur misinformation ka risk bahut zyada hai, isliye agency ko sirf essential tak limit karo.
SOURCESource: The Developer's Playbook for Large Language Model Security, O'Reilly, Chapter 7 — Trust No One
← Previous07.1 · Why Be So Paranoid?→ Next07.3 · Building Your Output Filter
07.3Chapter 7 · Trust No One

Building Your Output Filter

Output filter banana zero trust ka practical hissa hai — PII ko regex se pakdo, toxicity ko moderation API se score karo, dono filters ko LLM workflow se jodo, aur aakhir mein output ko sanitize karo. Ye section code-level approach deta hai.

Toxicity handle karna

  • Sentiment analysis: advanced algorithms text ka emotional tone evaluate karke negative sentiment pehchan sakte hain jo toxic content ki taraf ishara karta hai.
  • Keyword filtering: simple lekin kam sophisticated tareeka — pehle se bani offensive words ki list se flag ya replace karo. Dhyaan rakho: brute-force keyword filtering ke side effects hote hain — jaise "bomb" word block kar diya to bot history ke baare mein bhi baat nahi kar payega.
  • Custom ML models: toxicity ke liye labelled dataset par train kiya hua model zyada nuanced aur context-aware filtering deta hai — woh samajhta hai ki ek word ek context mein toxic hai, dusre mein nahi.

PII screen karna — kya-kya dhoondhna hai

  • PII ke types: Social Security number, credit card number, driver's license number, email address, phone number, home address, medical record aur financial information — ye sab leak hone par legal consequences aur reputation damage dono hote hain.
  • Regular expressions (regex): common format wali PII — email, phone, SSN — ke liye regex sabse simple tareeka hai, pattern match karke pakdo.
  • Named entity recognition (NER): advanced NLP technique jo text mein naam, address aur unique identifiers pehchan leti hai.
  • Dictionary-based matching: sensitive terms ki list se scan karo — lekin isme false positives zyada hote hain.
  • Machine learning models: specific context mein PII pehchanne ke liye custom model train karo, time ke saath accuracy badhti hai.
  • Data masking aur tokenization: pehchani hui PII ko placeholder ya token se replace kar do — data system ke kaam ka rahe, lekin malicious use ke liye bekaar ho jaye.
  • Contextual analysis: aas-paas ka text dekh kar decide karo ki ek string sach mein PII hai ya nahi — isse false positives kam hote hain.

Unforeseen execution rokna

  • HTML encoding: web context mein use karne se pehle LLM output ko HTML-encode karo, taaki active code neutral ho jaye aur XSS na ho.
  • Safe contextual insertion: agar output SQL query ka hissa bane to use data ki tarah treat karo, executable code ki tarah nahi — prepared statements ya parameterized queries use karo.
  • Syntax aur keywords limit karo: filtering layer mein dangerous programming syntax ya keywords ko remove ya escape karo.
  • Shell interpretable outputs disable karo: shell commands se interact karne wale output mein special meaning wale characters ko remove ya escape karo, shell injection ka chance kam karo.
  • Tokenization: output ko tokenize karke unsafe tokens filter karo — jaise <script> HTML tags ya DROP TABLE jaise SQL commands.

PII with regex — SSN example

  • Pattern: US Social Security number ka standard format hai XXX-XX-XXXX, jahan har X ek digit hai — Python mein re library se pattern \b\d{3}-\d{2}-\d{4}\b se match karo.
  • Function ka kaam: ek function input string mein SSN dhoondhta hai, mile to batata hai aur True return karta hai, na mile to False — simple pattern matching hai.
  • Limitation: ye invalid numbers ko nahi pakadta — jaise 000-00-0000 bhi pattern match kar jayega — isliye production mein extra validation add karo.
  • Full-featured option: zyada advanced PII detection ke liye commercial API use kar sakte ho, jaise Google Cloud Natural Language API ya Amazon Comprehend — lekin inke costs hote hain, free nahi hain.

Toxicity evaluate karna — Moderation API

  • Score 0 se 1: toxicity dhoondhna SSN dhoondhne se bahut complex hai — yahan OpenAI Moderation API use hoti hai, jo text ko 0 aur 1 ke beech ek toxicity score deti hai, zyada score matlab zyada toxic hone ki probability.
  • Threshold choose karo: sample workflow mein threshold 0.7 rakha gaya hai — score 0.7 se zyada ho to output unsafe mana jata hai. Apne use case ke hisaab se threshold adjust kar sakte ho.

Filters ko LLM se link karna — end-to-end workflow

  • Step 1 — response lo: prompt se LLM ka response generate karo, max tokens limit karo (example mein 100 tokens).
  • Step 2 — toxicity check: Moderation API se toxicity score nikalo.
  • Step 3 — PII check: regex se PII dhoondho.
  • Step 4 — decision: agar toxicity threshold se zyada ho ya PII mile to output unsafe hai — user ko mat do, warning do aur log karo. Dono check pass ho to hi output safe hai.
  • Step 5 — log everything: har interaction — prompt, LLM output, safe ya unsafe — ko log file mein likho. Ye debugging, security auditing aur regulatory compliance ke liye zaroori hai.

Sanitize for safety

  • html.escape: web interface par output return karne se pehle Python ke html module se html.escape(text) karo — ye XSS se bachata hai.
  • Order yaad rakho: sanitization tabhi karo jab output safe declare ho chuka ho — unsafe output ko sanitize karke bhi user ko mat do, use block karo aur log karo.
  • Customize karo: ye simplest version hai — production system ke liye apni needs ke hisaab se aur sanitization add karo.
Yaad rakho: Output filter ek baar bana kar bhoolne wali cheez nahi hai — ise production ke liye customize aur expand karo, threshold apne risk ke hisaab se set karo, aur har output ko log karo taaki baad mein audit ho sake.
Python — PII check — SSN regex with re (book Ch 7)
import re

def contains_ssn(input_string):
    # Define a regular expression pattern for a U.S. Social Security Number
    ssn_pattern = r'\b\d{3}-\d{2}-\d{4}\b'

    # Search for the pattern in the input string
    match = re.search(ssn_pattern, input_string)

    # Check if a match was found
    if match:
        print("Found a Social Security Number: {match.group(0)}")
        return True
    else:
        print("No Social Security Number found.")
        return False

# Test the function
contains_ssn("My Social Security Number is 123-45-6789.")
contains_ssn("No number here!")
Python — Toxicity check — OpenAI Moderation API (book Ch 7)
import openai

def check_toxicity(text):
  """
  Checks the toxicity of a text using the OpenAI Moderation API.

  Args:
    text: The text to check for toxicity.

  Returns:
    A toxicity score between 0 and 1, where a higher score indicates a
    higher probability of the text being toxic.
  """

  response = openai.Moderation.create(input=text)
  toxicity_score = response["results"][0]["confidence"]
  return toxicity_score

# Test the function
check_toxicity("You are stupid.")
Python — End-to-end output filter — toxicity + PII + logging (book Ch 7)
 import openai
 import json

 # Initialize the OpenAI API client
 openai.api_key = "your_openai_api_key_here"

 def check_toxicity(text):

   response = openai.Moderation.create(input=text)
   toxicity_score = response["results"][0]["confidence"]
   return toxicity_score

 def check_for_PII(text):

  ssn_pattern = r"\b\d{3}-\d{2}-\d{4}\b"
  return bool(re.search(ssn_pattern, text))

def get_LLM_response(prompt):

  model_engine = "text-davinci-002" # You can use other engines
  response = openai.Completion.create(
      engine=model_engine,
      prompt=prompt,
      max_tokens=100 # Limiting to 100 tokens for this example
  )

  return response.choices[0].text.strip()

def log_results(prompt, llm_output, is_safe):

  with open("llm_safety_log.txt", "a") as log_file:
    log_file.write(f"Prompt: {prompt}\n")
    log_file.write(f"LLM Output: {llm_output}\n")
    log_file.write(f"Is Safe: {is_safe}\n")
    log_file.write("=" * 50 + "\n")

if __name__ == "__main__":
  prompt = "Tell me your thoughts on universal healthcare."
  llm_output = get_LLM_response(prompt)

  toxicity_level = check_toxicity(llm_output)
  contains_PII = check_for_PII(llm_output)

  is_safe = True

  if toxicity_level > 0.7 or contains_PII:
    print("Warning: The output is not safe to return to the user.")
    is_safe = False
  else:
    print("The output is safe to return to the user.")

  log_results(prompt, llm_output, is_safe)
Python — Sanitize output — html.escape against XSS (book Ch 7)
import html

def sanitize_output(text):
    return html.escape(text)
Python — Wiring sanitization into the safety flow (book Ch 7)
if toxicity_level > 0.7 or contains_PII:
    print("Warning: The output is not safe to return to the user.")
    is_safe = False
else:
    print("The output is safe to return to the user.")
    llm_output = sanitize_output(llm_output)

log_results(prompt, llm_output, is_safe)

← Previous07.2 · Zero Trust Architecture Implement Karo→ Next08 · DoS Attacks
08Chapter 8 · Don't Lose Your Wallet

DoS Attacks

DoS attack ka goal service ko band kar dena hai — itni requests bhej do ki genuine users ke liye kuch bache hi nahi. LLM ke zamane mein DoS sirf availability ka issue nahi raha, ye resource exhaustion aur direct financial loss ka bhi issue ban gaya hai.

DoS kya hai aur kyun khatarnak hai?

  • Definition: DoS ek intentional effort hai kisi computer system, network ya application ko uske intended users ke liye unavailable bana dene ki — aam taur par requests se overwhelm karke.
  • Impact: downtime se financial loss hota hai, khaas taur par online transactions par dependent business ke liye; baar-baar hone par brand par trust khatm hota hai.
  • Cover for bigger attack: DoS kabhi-kabhi sirf distraction hota hai — IT staff ka dhyaan bhatka kar peeche se data breach ya malware injection kar diya jata hai.
  • LLM mein naya dimension: LLM resource-intensive hote hain, isliye DoS yahan sirf disruption nahi — resource exhaustion, degraded performance aur direct financial loss bhi lata hai.

Volume-based attacks

  • Kaise kaam karta hai: target ko massive traffic se overwhelm kar do — UDP floods, ICMP floods aur spoofed-packet floods se bandwidth hi kha jao, legitimate traffic ke liye jagah hi na bache.
  • DDoS — distributed version: ek source se nahi, multiple compromised systems se coordinated attack — infected devices ka network, jise botnet kehte hain, alag-alag jagah se flood karta hai.
  • Simple lekin effective: ye sabse straightforward type hai — brute force volume se kaam ho jata hai.

Protocol attacks

  • Kaise kaam karta hai: network layer ya transport layer ke protocols ki kamzori exploit karo — chhota sa traffic bhej kar bhi target par disproportionately bada load daal do.
  • SYN floods: TCP handshake exploit karo — attacker rapid succession mein SYN requests bhejta hai lekin final acknowledgment bhej kar handshake complete hi nahi karta, server ke resources atak jate hain.
  • Ping of death: IP protocol ki limit (65,535 bytes) se bade pings bhejo — purane systems oversized packets handle nahi kar pate the, freeze, crash ya reboot ho jate the.
  • Smurf attack: attacker network ke broadcast address par ICMP requests bhejta hai, return address mein victim ka IP spoof karke — broadcast network ke saare devices victim ko reply bhejte hain, traffic amplify ho jata hai.
  • Bachav: traffic filtering, rate limiting aur network configuration adjustments ka combination chahiye.

Application layer attacks

  • Kaise kaam karta hai: application layer ko target karo jahan web pages generate hote hain — server se itne resources maango ki woh legitimate requests serve hi na kar paye.
  • Kam resources, zyada effect: volume ya protocol attacks se kam resources chahiye hote hain, lekin targeted hone ki wajah se bahut effective hote hain.
  • HTTP flood: web server ko high volume mein HTTP requests se flood kar do, uski respond karne ki capacity khatm kar do, website genuine users ke liye inaccessible ho jaye.
  • Slowloris: attacker multiple HTTP connections kholta hai lekin unhe partial requests bhej kar dheere-dheere open rakhta hai — server ke resources consume hote rehte hain aur legitimate requests ke liye kuch bachta nahi.

Epic DoS attack — Dyn (October 2016)

  • Kya hua: Dyn, ek leading DNS provider, par massive DDoS attack hua — us time ke sabse impactful DDoS attacks mein se ek.
  • Weapon — IoT botnet: attackers ne compromised IoT devices — jaise digital cameras aur DVRs — ko Mirai malware se infect karke botnet bana liya aur Dyn ke servers ko flood kar diya.
  • Scale: traffic lagbhag 1.2 Tbps (terabits per second) tak pahunch gaya.
  • Ripple effect: Dyn ki DNS services down hone se Twitter, Netflix, PayPal aur Amazon jaise bade platforms Europe aur North America mein unavailable ho gaye — attack multiple waves mein hua, intermittent outages hote rahe.
  • Sabak: ek provider par attack poore internet ko hila sakta hai — supply chain aur shared infrastructure ka risk samjho.
Yaad rakho: DoS sirf "site down" ka issue nahi hai — ye financial loss, trust loss aur dusre attacks ke liye cover bhi hai. LLM apps mein to iska bill bhi aata hai, isliye availability ke saath cost ko bhi protect karna padta hai.
SOURCESource: The Developer's Playbook for Large Language Model Security, O'Reilly, Chapter 8 — Don't Lose Your Wallet
← Previous07.3 · Building Your Output Filter→ Next08.1 · Model DoS Attacks Targeting LLMs
08.1Chapter 8 · Don't Lose Your Wallet

Model DoS Attacks Targeting LLMs

Model DoS traditional DoS se alag hai — ye network ya server ko nahi, LLM ki apni unique vulnerabilities ko target karta hai. Model ki architecture hi uski kamzori ban jati hai: chhota sa input, bada sa compute bill.

Traditional vs model DoS

  • Traditional DoS: network aur server infrastructure ko target karta hai — volume, protocol ya application layer se.
  • Model DoS: LLM ki functionality ko compromise karna ya uske resources ko exhaust karna — model ki apni khaasiyat ko exploit karke.
  • Dono ka risk: web UI ya REST API se connected LLM app par traditional DoS bhi ho sakta hai aur model DoS bhi — dono ke liye alag defenses chahiye.

Scarce resource attacks

  • LLM resource-hungry hai: complex text generate karne ke liye LLM ko bahut compute chahiye — GPUs ya specialized AI accelerators, jo costly hain aur limited supply mein hain, cloud mein bhi.
  • Attacker ka kaam aasan: attacker baar-baar LLM se bade documents translate karwaye ya long-form content generate karwaye — automation ya bots se scale kar de to compute resources jaldi drain ho jate hain.
  • Translation service example: ek translation service par simple flood of translation requests — har request individually normal lagti hai, service ne wahi handle karne ke liye design kiya hai — lekin LLM processing itni heavy hai ki modest coordinated influx bhi resources ko disproportionately kha jata hai.
  • Asymmetry: request bhejne mein attacker ka negligible effort lagta hai, lekin process karne mein system ka substantial load — ye gap hi exploitation ki wajah hai. Ek attacker bhi, modest resources se, service ko slow ya bilkul band kar sakta hai.

Context window exhaustion

  • Context window kya hai: transformer architecture mein attention mechanism model ko input ke alag-alag parts par focus karne deta hai — context window uski short-term memory hai, ye define karta hai ki model ek time par kitna text "yaad" rakh sakta hai.
  • Bina iske kya hota: context window ke bina LLM stateless ho jayega — jaise bina yaad ke conversation karna — coherent, context-aware response dena mushkil ho jayega.
  • Attack kaise hota hai: attacker bahut lambe prompts bhej kar ya aise prompts bana kar jo bahut verbose answers generate karein, context window ko bhar deta hai — maintain aur process karne ka computational demand bahut zyada hai, resources strain ho jate hain.
  • Cost bhi badhta hai: context window bharna sirf performance nahi, cost bhi badhata hai — har token ka paisa lagta hai.

Unpredictable user input

  • Problem: LLM varied queries ka jawab dene ke liye designed hai — attacker iska fayda utha kar complex, resource-intensive tasks karwa sakta hai.
  • Computationally intensive requests: jaise "1 billion tak ke saare prime numbers ka sum kya hai?" — poochhna aasan hai, lekin itne bade range mein primality check karna bahut heavy computation hai.
  • Extensive content generation: jaise "har World Cup match ka detailed history likho" — hundreds of events ko ek comprehensive narrative mein jodna, har token generation mein compute lagta hai, lamba response system ko tax kar deta hai.
  • Complex reasoning chains: jaise "smartphone banane ke har step ko mining se final assembly tak explain karo, har stage ke socioeconomic impacts ke saath" — multiple knowledge domains ko deep causal chains se jodna, generative task ki complexity aur duration dono badh jati hai.
  • Chhota input, bada kaam: "one million factorial kya hai?" likhne mein kuch dozen bytes lagte hain, lekin execute karne mein one million multiplications — aur upar wale examples to usse bhi zyada heavy hain. Bina safeguards ke LLM boundless computational journeys par nikal sakta hai.
Yaad rakho: Model DoS mein attacker ko botnet ya advanced technique ki zaroorat nahi — LLM ki deep, thoughtful analysis wali design hi uski Achilles' heel hai. Isliye input size, output size aur compute per request par limits lagana zaroori hai.
SOURCESource: The Developer's Playbook for Large Language Model Security, O'Reilly, Chapter 8 — Don't Lose Your Wallet
← Previous08 · DoS Attacks→ Next08.2 · DoW Attacks aur Model Cloning
08.2Chapter 8 · Don't Lose Your Wallet

DoW Attacks aur Model Cloning

DoW attack service ko band nahi karta, wallet ko khaali karta hai — pay-per-use pricing ko exploit karke victim ka bill unsustainable level tak badha deta hai. Model cloning usi repeated querying ka use karke tumhari intellectual property chura leta hai.

DoW attacks — denial of wallet

  • DoS se farq: traditional DoS availability ko target karta hai, DoW financial resources ko — goal hai organization ko economic damage pahunchana, usage-based pricing ko exploit karke costs ko unsustainable bana dena.
  • History: DoW naya nahi hai — pehle cloud services mein compute time, data transfer ya transaction volume se cost badha kar hota tha. LLM ke zamane mein ye aur prominent ho gaya hai.
  • LLM kyun vulnerable hai: high computational costs, scalability of usage, API-based access aur expensive, complex pricing models — ye chaaro milkar LLM ko DoW ke liye perfect target banate hain.

LLM ko DoW-prone banane wale chaar factors

  • High computational costs: text generation, translation ya data analysis ke liye significant processing power chahiye — cloud deployment mein iska matlab higher operational cost.
  • Scalability of usage: LLM apps requests ke volume ke saath scale karne ke liye designed hain — attacker is scalability ko exploit karke resource consumption aur cost ko rapidly badha sakta hai.
  • API-based access: LLM aksar APIs se access hote hain — attacker programmatically high volume mein requests generate karke cost badha sakta hai, manually karne ki zaroorat nahi.
  • Expensive, complex pricing models: pricing tokens processed, interaction ki duration ya model ke type jaise multiple factors par based hoti hai — attacker in characteristics ko use karke financial impact maximize kar sakta hai.

Advanced DoW — tumhare kharche par attacker ka kaam

  • Prompt injection se takeover: attacker pehle prompt injection se guardrails todta hai, phir LLM ko apne nefarious kaam ke liye use karta hai — tumhare kharche par. Example: hijacked LLM se phishing emails generate karwana ya CAPTCHA puzzles crack karwana, ek bade hacking campaign ke hisse ke taur par.
  • Cryptojacking se comparison: cryptojacking mein attacker victim ke cloud resources se cryptocurrency mine karta hai — victim ka cost badhta hai, attacker ko profit hota hai. Advanced DoW mein bhi yahi hota hai, lekin ek extra khatra hai.
  • Legal liability: cryptojacking mein sirf financial loss hota hai, lekin hijacked LLM se illegal kaam karwaya jaye to victim par additional legal liability bhi aa sakti hai — aur wallet to khaali hoga hi.

Model cloning — intellectual property ki chori

  • Kaise kaam karta hai: attacker specific topics par vast array of prompts se LLM ko strategically query karta hai, outputs record karta hai, aur un outputs se apna alternate model fine-tune kar leta hai — original LLM ki functionality aur knowledge base ko replicate kar leta hai, bina uski architecture ya training data tak direct access ke.
  • Synthetic training data: model se generate karwaya hua data hi attacker ke naye model ki training data ban jata hai — tumhara model, tumhare kharche par, attacker ke model ko train kar raha hai.
  • DoS/DoW se similarity: cloning ke liye bhi repeated queries chahiye hoti hain, bilkul DoS attacks ki tarah — isliye inke defenses bhi kaafi had tak same hain.
  • Intent mein farq: DoS ka goal service disrupt karna hai, cloning ka goal covertly model ki capabilities ko copy karna hai — ye intellectual property ka direct threat hai aur proprietary technology tak unauthorized access ka rasta khol sakta hai.
Yaad rakho: DoW mein nuksaan sirf downtime ka nahi, bill ka hai — aur advanced DoW mein bill ke saath legal trouble bhi. Model cloning mein nuksaan tumhari mehnat se bani IP ka hai. Dono ko rokne ke liye repeated-query pattern ko pehchanna aur rokna zaroori hai.
SOURCESource: The Developer's Playbook for Large Language Model Security, O'Reilly, Chapter 8 — Don't Lose Your Wallet
← Previous08.1 · Model DoS Attacks Targeting LLMs→ Next08.3 · Mitigation Strategies
08.3Chapter 8 · Don't Lose Your Wallet

Mitigation Strategies

DoS, DoW aur model cloning se bachne ke liye ek hi defense kaafi nahi — domain guardrails, input validation, rate limiting, resource capping, monitoring aur financial thresholds, ye saare layers milkar kaam karte hain. Aur sabse pehle prompt injection ko rokna zaroori hai, kyunki kai attacks wahi se shuru hote hain.

Pehle prompt injection roko

  • Attack ki shuruaat: kai DoS ya DoW attacks prompt injection se shuru hote hain — attacker pehle jailbreak karke tumhare lagaye hue guardrails ko todta hai, phir system ka misuse karta hai.
  • Isliye Chapter 4 wali strategies follow karo: prompt injection mitigation ke tareeke yahan bhi apply hote hain — lekin ye bhi yaad rakho ki prompt injection ko poori tarah nullify karna mushkil hai, isliye dusre safeguards bhi zaroori hain.
  • Defense in depth: ek layer fail ho to dusri layer pakde — sirf ek defense par bharosa mat karo.

Domain-specific guardrails

  • Kya karna hai: model ko fine-tune karo taaki woh sirf domain-specific inquiries ka jawab de — alignment ka matlab hai AI system ke objectives ko developer ke intended values, goals aur safety considerations se match karna.
  • Example: ecommerce website ka chatbot sirf purchases aur product details ke baare mein jawab de, complex maths jaise unrelated queries ko deflect kare.
  • Dual benefit: processing power efficiently use hoti hai, aur resource-draining irrelevant inputs se excessive cost ka risk kam hota hai.

Input validation aur sanitization

  • Strict criteria set karo: acceptable input ke liye clear standards banao aur har incoming data ko un standards se rigorously check karo.
  • Sanitization: data mein se potentially harmful elements ko actively remove ya neutralize karo.
  • Context window se bada input: truncate karo ya divide karo — poora ka poora heavy input model ko mat do.
  • Unusual ya complex structures: aise inputs jo excessive processing karwayein, unhe simplify karo ya reject karo — isse resource-intensive operations ka risk kam hota hai aur LLM ki integrity aur performance bani rehti hai.

Robust rate limiting

  • Kya karna hai: define aur enforce karo ki ek user ya system ek time frame mein kitni baar LLM ko request kar sakta hai — requests ki sankhya ya processed data ki matra par sensible thresholds set karo.
  • Deliberate attack ho ya legitimate surge: dono mein rate limiting system ko overwhelm hone se bachata hai.
  • Sophisticated rate limiting: dynamic adjustments bhi karo — ongoing system performance aur user behavior ki monitoring ke basis par limits ko flexible aur responsive banao.

Resource use capping

  • Per query cap: har query ya processing step par resource use cap karo — tokens per request, computation ki complexity ya single input ke liye allowed time par limit lagao.
  • Attacker ke liye mushkil: cap lagne se attacker ke liye LLM se highly resource-intensive task karwana mushkil ho jata hai.
  • Predictable performance: high load mein bhi system ka performance predictable aur stable rehta hai.

Monitoring aur alerts

  • Kya track karo: CPU usage, memory consumption, response times aur concurrent requests ki sankhya — in metrics ki continuous monitoring karo.
  • Baseline banao: normal operation ka baseline pattern establish karo, taaki anomaly aasani se detect ho — baseline se deviation hi attack ka pehla signal hota hai.
  • Alerting system: robust alerting rakho taaki unusual activity turant relevant personnel tak pahunche, quick investigation aur response ho sake — proactive approach se attack ka impact minimize hota hai aur service reliable rehti hai.
  • Regular audits: stringent access controls, regular security audits aur real-time anomaly detection systems — ye teeno milkar unauthorized access ya unusual activity se protect karte hain.

Financial thresholds aur alerts

  • Budget limits set karo: cloud-based LLM usage ke liye budget limits establish karo aur alerts configure karo jo administrators ko notify karein jab thresholds approach ho ya exceed ho jayein.
  • Pay-per-use mein critical: jahan cost seedha usage se judi ho, wahan ye measures DoW attack ka damage drastically kam kar dete hain.
  • Close monitoring: usage costs ko closely monitor karo aur predefined limits rakho, taaki malicious exploitation se unexpected financial burden na aaye.
Yaad rakho: Mitigation ek checklist nahi, ek layered system hai — guardrails + validation + rate limiting + capping + monitoring + financial alerts, sab ek saath. Koi ek layer chhooti to attacker wahi gap dhoondh lega.
SOURCESource: The Developer's Playbook for Large Language Model Security, O'Reilly, Chapter 8 — Don't Lose Your Wallet
← Previous08.2 · DoW Attacks aur Model Cloning→ Next09 · Supply Chain Basics
09Chapter 9 · Find the Weakest Link

Supply Chain Basics

Supply chain ka matlab hai product banane aur deliver karne ki poori process — raw material se lekar end user tak. Software mein ye chain aur bhi complex hai, aur ek chhota sa weak link poori chain ko tod sakta hai — jaise Equifax, SolarWinds aur Log4Shell ne dikhaya.

Supply chain kya hai?

  • Definition: supply chain mein procurement, manufacturing, transportation aur distribution aate hain — suppliers, manufacturers aur retailers ka network milkar product ko end user tak pahunchata hai.
  • Real-world example: ek specific semiconductor ki shortage ek jagah par poori iPhone production rok sakti hai; ek seat belt component fail ho to Ford jaisi company ko massive safety recall karna padta hai.
  • Weakest link: kahawat hai — chain utni hi strong hoti hai jitna uska sabse kamzor link. Ek weak point poore system ko fail kar sakta hai — security, teamwork aur quality assurance, har jagah yehi principle lagta hai.

Software supply chain security

  • Kya hai: software ki integrity aur security ensure karne ke measures, development se deployment tak — third-party components ko vulnerabilities ke liye scrutinize karna, code repositories ko secure karna, aur CI/CD processes ko safeguard karna.
  • Software factories: badi software teams ko aaj software factories kaha jata hai kyunki large-scale development mass production jaisa ho gaya hai — isliye supply chain concept yahan bhi bilkul relevant hai.
  • Kyun zaroori hai: supply chain mein ek breach se severe data breach, customer trust ka loss aur significant financial aur reputational damage ho sakta hai.
  • Kya karna hai: third-party components ki rigorous vetting, saare elements ki up-to-date inventory (aksar SBOM ke through), vulnerabilities ke liye regular scanning, aur ek comprehensive proactive approach.

The Equifax Breach (2017)

  • Vulnerability: March 2017 mein Apache Struts web framework mein serious vulnerability disclose hui (CVE-2017-5638) — malicious input se remote code execution, maximum severity score 10.
  • Galti: Equifax, ek badi consumer credit reporting agency, apne public web portal mein Struts use karti thi lekin disclose hone ke do mahine se zyada tak patch nahi lagaya.
  • Breach: May 2017 mein hackers ne unpatched flaw exploit karke 148 million consumers ka sensitive personal aur financial data exfiltrate kar liya — breach July 2017 mein discover hua, losses $1 billion se zyada.
  • Impact: SSN, address aur birth dates chori hone se identity theft; multiple class-action lawsuits; hundreds of millions dollars ka settlement; senior executives fire hue aur reputation ko bada damage.
  • Lessons: open source components ko jaldi patch karo, khaas taur par internet-facing; external attack surface aur third-party risks samjho; breach impact limit karne ke liye multilayer security controls use karo; incident response planning "if" ke liye nahi, "when" ke liye karo.

The SolarWinds Hack (December 2020)

  • Kya hua: hackers ne SolarWinds Orion network monitoring software mein malicious code insert kar diya, jo March se June 2020 ke beech software updates ke roop mein customers tak pahunch gaya — customers ko pata bhi nahi chala.
  • Scale: US government agencies, Microsoft aur FireEye jaise bade tech companies aur corporations target hue — 100 se zyada US companies aur government agencies affected.
  • Stealth: attackers ne lagbhag ek saal tak detection avoid ki, legitimate user activity ko impersonate karke aur normal network traffic mein blend hokar.
  • Impact: sensitive government aur corporate data theft, core infrastructure aur internal communications tak access, interconnected partners mein cascading breaches, incident response aur remediation ke significant costs.
  • Lessons: multifactor authentication, privileged access management aur logging se unusual access detect karo; vendors software verification, code audits aur enhanced supply chain controls karein; systems ke beech compartmentalization badhao taaki lateral movement limit ho; breach assume karke proactive threat hunting karo; public aur private sector mein faster coordination aur information sharing karo.
  • Build pipeline ka sabak: attackers ne SolarWinds ki build pipeline compromise ki thi — apni build pipelines ko secure karna crucial hai, failure ka impact sirf tum par nahi, tumhare customers par bhi padta hai.

The Log4Shell Vulnerability (November 2021)

  • Kya hua: Log4j, ek Java logging library jo incredible sankhya mein applications mein use hoti hai, mein critical zero-day remote code execution vulnerability mili (CVE-2021-44228, naam Log4Shell).
  • Zero-day kya hai: aisa unknown flaw jo developers ke patch banane se pehle saamne aa jaye — zero days to prepare — isliye attackers fix aane se pehle hi exploit kar sakte hain.
  • Kaise exploit hui: Log4j mein improper input validation thi — crafted requests se server par malicious Java code execute ho jata tha. Attackers internet, SMS aur chat apps se payloads bhej sakte the — jab untrusted input innocently Log4j mein log hota, to attacker ko server ka full shell access mil jata tha, isiliye naam Log4Shell.
  • Impact: disclosure ke kuch dinon mein millions of internet-facing systems scan hue — botnets, cryptominers, ransomware groups aur state-sponsored hackers ne exploit kiya. Data theft, malware/backdoors/cryptominers ki installation, ransomware se operations band, cascading supply chain breaches, aur cloud aur on-prem infrastructure mein urgent out-of-cycle patching.
  • Lessons: open source components benefits ke saath massive systemic risks bhi late hain; libraries mein input validation aur security hygiene par zyada dhyaan do; vulnerabilities ki rapid coordination aur disclosure important hai; SBOM component risks samajhne mein madad karta hai; suppliers ko sirf exploit rokne par nahi, breach assume karke intrusion hunt karne par bhi focus karna chahiye.
Yaad rakho: Ye teenon breaches ek hi baat sikhate hain — tumhara code kitna bhi achha ho, agar tumhe nahi pata ki tumhare software mein kya-kya components hain aur unme kya vulnerabilities hain, to ek unpatched library poori company ko gira sakti hai.
SOURCESource: The Developer's Playbook for Large Language Model Security, O'Reilly, Chapter 9 — Find the Weakest Link

09.1Chapter 9 · Find the Weakest Link

Understanding the LLM Supply Chain

LLM ki supply chain normal software se alag hai — isme sirf code aur libraries nahi, massive training datasets, foundation models, external APIs aur plug-ins bhi aate hain. Har ek dependency ek naya attack surface hai.

LLM supply chain kyun unique hai?

  • Massive aur diverse datasets: LLM training ke liye bahut bade aur alag-alag datasets chahiye hote hain — data hi yahan raw material hai, aur data mein poison ho to model mein poison aa jata hai.
  • Foundation model dependency: third-party foundation model integrate karna sirf software component ki dependency nahi hai — us model ko banane mein use hua data bhi tumhari supply chain ka hissa ban jata hai.
  • Updates track karo: model ke updates, patches aur changes ko track karna crucial hai — ek update tumhare app ki performance aur security dono ko significantly affect kar sakta hai.
  • Fine-tuning ka data bhi count karo: pretrained model ko fine-tune karte ho to fine-tuning ke liye use hua training data bhi supply chain mein aata hai.
  • RAG aur external integration: RAG use karne wale LLMs external APIs, databases aur online resources se interact karte hain — real-time info ke liye ye zaroori hai, lekin isse security vulnerabilities, data privacy concerns aur compliance issues ke naye vectors khul jate hain.

Open source model risk

  • Choice: kai teams proprietary hosted model use karti hain, lekin aur zyada teams open source foundation models ke saath experiment kar rahi hain — agar tum model manage aur host karte ho to uska version aur configuration supply chain mein track hona chahiye.
  • Hugging Face — model exchange ki sabse popular jagah: yahan models, datasets aur applications share hote hain, lekin iski supply chain highly immature hai — malicious actor aasani se tainted model daal sakta hai.
  • July 2023 incident: ek malicious user ne reused employee passwords (jo dusri site ke data breach mein compromise hue the) se Meta aur Intel ki Hub organizations par control le liya — isse ye dikh gaya ki trusted source se aaya hua component bhi badla ja sakta hai.
  • December 2023 — token leak: research mein dikhaya gaya ki 1,600 se zyada Hugging Face API tokens expose the, jinse 700 se zyada organizations ke accounts access kiye ja sakte the — jinme Meta, Microsoft, Google aur VMware jaise bade players bhi the. Matlab ek well-known, well-trusted model ko attacker apne modifications wale model se swap kar sakta hai — ye massive risk hai.
  • Pickle ka khatra: Pickle, machine learning mein serialization ke liye commonly use hota hai aur PyTorch mein model weights ka default format hai — Hugging Face ki documentation warn karti hai ki tainted Pickle files load karne se arbitrary code execution ho sakta hai. Iske solution ke taur par Safetensors project develop ho raha hai, jo abhi early stages mein hai lekin follow karne layak hai.

Training data poisoning

  • Kya hai: training data ko manipulate karke LLM mein vulnerability daal dena — falsified information inject karke, data ko bias karke ya adversarial examples bana kar — goal hai model se inaccurate ya harmful outputs nikalwana.
  • Purana problem: spammers ne Gmail ke spam filters ko train karne wale data ko poison karne ki baar-baar koshish ki hai — ye concept naya nahi hai.
  • Sirf $60 mein: early 2023 mein research ne dikhaya ki sirf $60 kharch karke researchers Wikipedia jaise resources mein data insert kar sakte hain jo internet-scale training results ko influence kar sake.
  • Datasets bhi target hain: Hugging Face par 250,000 se zyada prebuilt datasets hain jo developers train ya fine-tune ke liye use karte hain — datasets ko bhi models ki tarah manipulate kiya ja sakta hai, isliye fine-tuning datasets ko track karna foundation model ko track karne jitna hi important hai.

Accidentally unsafe training data

  • Galti se bhi ho sakta hai: data poisoning mein malicious actor actively kaam karta hai, lekin unsafe data galti se bhi aa sakta hai — khaas taur par jab training datasets public internet sources se liye gaye hon.
  • LAION-5B example: December 2023 mein research ne dikhaya ki ek highly popular dataset (LAION-5B), jo image generation algorithms train karne mein use hota tha, mein 3,000 se zyada images related to child sexual abuse material the.
  • Impact: AI image generation tools ke developers ko scramble karna pada ye determine karne ke liye ki unke models ne ye training data use kiya tha ya nahi aur iska kya impact hoga.
  • Documentation ki importance: agar development team ne carefully document nahi kiya ki unhone kaunsa training data use kiya, to unhe pata hi nahi chalega ki unke models inappropriate aur illegal images generate karne ke risk mein hain ya nahi.

Unsafe plug-ins

  • March 2023 — plug-ins launch: OpenAI ne plug-ins ke through third-party functionalities add ki — Expedia, Zillow, Kayak, Instacart aur OpenTable jaise providers se — job searching, real estate, shopping, gaming aur recipe retrieval jaise kaam possible hue, utility aur engagement dono badhe.
  • Risks: researchers ne jaldi hi security concerns pehchane — plug-ins ko ChatGPT sessions mein malicious code inject karne ke vector ki tarah use kiya ja sakta hai, jisse data theft, malware installation ya user ke computer par full control bhi ho sakta hai.
  • Unauthorized data collection: ek plug-in user ki browsing activities track kar sakta hai ya ChatGPT ke saath conversations record kar sakta hai, bina user ki knowledge ya consent ke — bada privacy concern.
  • Kya karna hai: plug-ins ke sources aur versions ko meticulously track karo, vulnerabilities ke liye continuous monitoring, regular updates aur comprehensive security audits karo — users ka trust aur safety maintain karne ke liye ye vigilance vital hai.
Yaad rakho: Tumhare models, training data aur RAG se access kiya hua data — ye sab tumhari software supply chain ka hissa hain. Har dependency ko track karo taaki vulnerability discover hone par turant action le sako.
SOURCESource: The Developer's Playbook for Large Language Model Security, O'Reilly, Chapter 9 — Find the Weakest Link

09.2Chapter 9 · Find the Weakest Link

SBOMs aur Artifacts

SBOM ek software ki ingredient list hai — usme kya-kya components, libraries aur modules hain, sab likha hota hai. Jab tumhe pata ho ki tumhare software mein kya hai, tabhi tum vulnerability aane par turant pata laga sakte ho ki tum affected ho ya nahi.

SBOM kya hai?

  • Definition: software bill of materials ek comprehensive inventory hai — ek detailed list jisme software ke saare components, libraries aur modules hote hain. Ye manufacturing ke bill of materials (BOM) se aaya hai — BOM mein product banane ke liye chahiye hui saari materials, components aur sub-assemblies ki list hoti hai, part names, numbers aur quantities ke saath.
  • Kya include hota hai: team ka likha hua code bhi aur integrated open source ya third-party components bhi — sab kuch.
  • Purpose: software ki composition mein clear visibility dena — security, compliance aur management ke liye crucial hai.
  • Rapid response: SBOM se organizations vulnerabilities ko monitor kar sakti hain, legal aur licensing requirements comply kar sakti hain, aur updates aur patches ko effectively manage kar sakti hain — aur jab naya vulnerability disclose ho to turant pata chal jata hai ki tumhara software affected hai ya nahi, attacker ka window kam ho jata hai.
  • Compliance proof: SBOM due diligence ka proof bhi hai — ye dikhata hai ki tumne secure aur licensed components use kiye hain.

Model cards — Hugging Face ka standard artifact

  • Kya hai: model card ek standardized artifact hai jo Hugging Face par hosted har AI model ke baare mein comprehensive information deta hai — taaki developers, researchers aur end users ko model ki capabilities, limitations aur intended use cases ki clear understanding mile.
  • Model description: model ka purpose, architecture aur training data — high-level understanding ke liye.
  • Training data: model ko train karne mein kaunse datasets use hue — isse model ke potential biases aur limitations samajhne mein madad milti hai.
  • Intended use: model kis context mein achha perform karega, aur use karne ki recommendations ya guidelines kya hain.
  • Ethical considerations: model mein potential biases aur deployment ka alag-alag stakeholders par impact — responsible AI ki taraf ek kadam.
  • Performance metrics: benchmark datasets ya specific tasks par model kaisa perform karta hai.
  • Limitations: model kahan expected jaisa perform nahi karega, kin applications mein risk hai, kahan caution se use karna hai — ye sabse critical sections mein se ek hai.
  • Usage examples aur tutorials: code snippets ya notebooks ke links ke saath model ko integrate karne ke examples.
  • Fragmentation: dusre vendors, jaise AWS, ne apne model card formats develop karne shuru kar diye hain — is space mein fragmentation hoga, har project ke liye kaunsa format use karna hai ye sochna padega, lekin conceptually sab similar hain.

Model cards vs SBOMs — farq samjho

  • Purpose aur focus: model card ka primary purpose hai ML model ki capabilities, behavior aur limitations ko clearly describe karna — performance, ethical considerations, use cases aur training data par focus. SBOM ka focus hai software product ke har component ki detailed inventory — vulnerabilities, licenses aur dependencies track karna.
  • Content: model cards mein model architecture, training data, performance metrics, intended use, ethical considerations aur limitations hote hain. SBOMs mein har software component, version, patch status, licenses aur kabhi-kabhi origin bhi hota hai.
  • Security aur compliance mein use: model cards directly security vulnerabilities address nahi karte, lekin indirectly model ki robustness aur reliability indicate karte hain. SBOMs directly vulnerability management mein use hote hain — security team turant identify kar sakti hai ki newly discovered vulnerability unke software ko affect karti hai ya nahi — license compliance aur risk management mein bhi.
  • Industry application: model cards AI/ML specific hain, responsible AI movement ka hissa. SBOMs broadly saare software development mein applicable hain aur security aur compliance wali industries mein standard documentation ban rahe hain.
  • Dono chahiye: dono transparency badhate hain lekin alag purpose serve karte hain — kai situations mein dono ki zaroorat padegi, jab tak koi single comprehensive structure develop nahi hota.
Yaad rakho: SBOM tumhara map hai — bina map ke tumhe pata hi nahi chalega ki Log4Shell jaisa vulnerability tumhe affect karta hai ya nahi. Inventory pehle banao, patching baad mein aasan ho jayegi.
SOURCESource: The Developer's Playbook for Large Language Model Security, O'Reilly, Chapter 9 — Find the Weakest Link
← Previous09.1 · Understanding the LLM Supply Chain→ Next09.3 · Model Cards, CycloneDX aur ML-BOM
09.3Chapter 9 · Find the Weakest Link

Model Cards, CycloneDX aur ML-BOM

CycloneDX OWASP ka SBOM standard hai, aur uska version 1.5 ML-BOM le kar aaya — machine learning bill of materials — jo models, datasets, training pipelines aur frameworks ko bhi SBOM mein list karta hai. Sample ML-BOM se samjho ki ye practical mein kaisa dikhta hai.

CycloneDX — SBOM standard

  • Kya hai: CycloneDX, OWASP Foundation ke under managed, SBOMs ke liye sabse powerful standard hai — ek standardized format jo project ya system ke saare software components ki structured, machine-readable inventory deta hai, unke relationships aur dependencies ke details ke saath.
  • Kyun bana: software dependencies ki complexity badhne se security aur compliance challenges badh gaye the — CycloneDX software composition ko clearly outline karke vulnerabilities identify karne aur risks manage karne ki ability badhata hai.
  • Standardization ka fayda: CycloneDX se pehle alag-alag tools alag SBOM formats use karte the, sharing aur interoperability mushkil thi — CycloneDX ek unified language deta hai, tools aur platforms mein seamless integration hoti hai.
  • Open source aur community-driven: OWASP ke under open source project hai, community ke through continuously evolve hota hai aur sabke liye accessible hai.
  • Compliance: US Executive Order on Improving the Nation's Cybersecurity jaise regulations government software ke liye SBOMs mandate karte hain — CycloneDX in requirements ko meet karne mein instrumental hai. License management mein bhi madad karta hai — har component ki license info store hoti hai, legal entanglements se bachne mein madad milti hai.
  • DevOps integration: DevOps aur CI processes mein CycloneDX ko incorporate karke SBOM generation automate ho jata hai — development lifecycle mein ongoing insights milti rehti hain, aur SBOM share karne se users aur customers mein trust badhta hai.

ML-BOM ka rise — CycloneDX 1.5 (June 2023)

  • Kya hai ML-BOM: machine learning bill of materials — CycloneDX 1.5 ki key innovation, jo SBOM mein ML models, algorithms, datasets, training pipelines aur frameworks ko comprehensively list karne ki facility deti hai.
  • Kya capture hota hai: model provenance, versioning, dependencies aur performance metrics — reproducibility, governance, risk assessment aur compliance ke liye zaroori details.
  • Transparency: ML development aur deployment ke components aur processes mein clear visibility milti hai — stakeholders system ki composition samajh sakte hain, potential risks identify kar sakte hain aur ethical implications consider kar sakte hain.
  • Security: ML components aur dependencies mein vulnerabilities identify aur remedy kar sakte ho — security audits aur risk assessments ke liye essential hai.
  • Compliance: GDPR aur CCPA jaise regulatory requirements ke adherence mein support karta hai — transparency aur governance ensure karke, compliance audits aur responsible AI practices demonstrate karne mein madad karta hai.
  • Extra benefits: reproducibility (experiments aur results replicate kar sakte ho), collaboration (teams aur organizations mein sharing aasan), aur knowledge management (future maintenance, updates aur audits ke liye critical info preserve rehti hai).

Sample ML-BOM — Customer Service Bot

  • Scenario: ek LLM-based application "Customer Service Bot" — Mixtral-8x7B-v0.1 foundation model Hugging Face se download kiya, phir GitHub se liye hue open source customer service dataset se fine-tune kiya.
  • Application component: type Application, name Customer Service Bot, version 1.0.0, description — ek customer service bot, external reference (VCS) Hugging Face par Mixtral-8x7B-v0.1 ka link.
  • Dataset component: type Dataset, name Customer Support LLM Chatbot Training Dataset, version 1.0.0, licenses — CDLA-Sharing-1.0 aur Apache 2.0, external references — GitHub par dataset ka VCS link aur license file ka direct link.
  • Machine-readable JSON: human-readable table concepts samjhata hai, lekin SBOM/ML-BOM ki asli taakat ye hai ki woh highly structured aur machine-readable ho — CycloneDX standard JSON format deta hai jisme bomFormat (CycloneDX), specVersion (1.5), version (1) aur components array hota hai, har component mein type, name, version, description, licenses aur externalReferences hote hain.
  • VCS ka matlab: ML-BOM mein VCS tag ka matlab version control system hai — diya hua URL woh repository hai jahan component ka source code, model ya related data manage aur store hota hai.
  • Accurate details bharo: components aur externalReferences sections mein apne specific use case ki accurate details bharo — baaki dependencies, services ya training data bhi include karo.

Model card vs ML-BOM — summary

  • Purpose: model card — ML model ki ethical considerations, intended use aur performance document karna; ML-BOM — ML system ke saare components list karke application ko manage aur secure karna.
  • Components listed: model card mein model details, performance metrics aur ethical considerations; ML-BOM mein ML models, algorithms, datasets, training pipelines aur frameworks.
  • Security details: model card mein general ethical considerations aur use case limitations; ML-BOM mein detailed security vulnerabilities, dependencies aur versioning.
  • Usage context: model card primarily model evaluation aur deployment stages par; ML-BOM poore development aur deployment lifecycle mein.
  • Focus: dono mein transparency high hai — model card ethical transparency par, ML-BOM security aur compliance par focus karta hai.
Yaad rakho: Model cards aur ML-BOMs mein overlap hai lekin details mein substantial farq hai — kai situations mein dono ki zaroorat padegi. CycloneDX 1.5 use karo taaki tum growing tooling ecosystem ka fayda utha sako.
JSON — CycloneDX 1.5 ML-BOM for Customer Service Bot (book Ch 9)
{
    "bomFormat": "CycloneDX",
    "specVersion": "1.5",
    "version": 1,
    "components": [
      {
        "type": "application",
        "name": "Customer Service Bot",

               "version": "1.0.0",
               "description": "A customer service bot built for company XYZ",
               "externalReferences": [
                 {
                   "type": "vcs",
                   "url": "https://huggingface.co/mistralai/Mixtral-8x7B-v0.1"
                 }
               ]
           },
           {
               "type": "dataset",
               "name": "Customer Support LLM Chatbot Training Dataset",
               "version": "1.0.0",
               "licenses": [
                 {
                    "license": {
                       "name": "Apache 2.0",
                       "url": "https://choosealicense.com/licenses/apache-2.0/"
                     }
                  }
               ],
               "externalReferences": [
                  {
                     "type": "vcs",
                     "url": "https://github.com/bitext/customer-support-dataset"
                  },
                  {
                     "type": "license",
                     "url": "https://github.com/bitext/customer-support-dataset/LICENSE.txt"
                  }
               ]
           }
      ]
  }
SOURCESource: The Developer's Playbook for Large Language Model Security, O'Reilly, Chapter 9 — Find the Weakest Link

09.4Chapter 9 · Find the Weakest Link

Future of LLM Supply Chain Security

LLM supply chain security abhi immature hai — web apps ke liye ye field mature hai, lekin AI ke liye abhi standards ban rahe hain. Aage digital signing, watermarking aur AI-specific vulnerability databases is space ko mature karenge.

Digital signing aur watermarking

  • Kyun zaroori hai: models proliferate ho rahe hain, isliye ye validate karna critical ho gaya hai ki model expected source se aaya hai aur uske saath tampering nahi hui hai — accountability aur security ke liye.
  • Digital signatures: model ko private key se cryptographically sign karo — koi bhi party corresponding public key se verify kar sakti hai ki signature model se match karta hai, provenance aur integrity prove hoti hai. Models jab systems ke beech move karte hain ya cloud services se deploy hote hain, signing se unhe authenticate kiya ja sakta hai.
  • Watermarking: identifying information ko seedha model ke weights ya architecture mein embed kar do — unique fingerprint jo model ki origin batata hai, parameters ko subtly alter karke. Watermark duplication ke baad bhi survive karta hai, isliye cloned ya stolen models mein bhi markup rehta hai — extraction tool se detect karke confirm kiya ja sakta hai ki watermark expected signature se match karta hai.
  • Dono ek saath: signatures origin validate karte hain aur tampering rokte hain (cryptography se), watermarks cloned models mein bhi origin trace karne dete hain — dono techniques tumhare arsenal mein honi chahiye.
  • Sigstore aur SLSA: kuch researchers Sigstore tool aur SLSA (Supply-chain Levels for Software Artifacts) framework ka combination promote kar rahe hain ML models ko sign aur manage karne ke liye — abhi standardized approaches kam hain, isliye is combination ke evolution par nazar rakho.
  • C2PA: Coalition for Content Provenance and Authenticity (C2PA) content authenticity ke standards develop karne mein leader hai — latest resources aur standards ke liye use follow karo, kyunki ye technology tezi se evolve hoti hai.

Vulnerability classifications aur databases

  • Classifications kya hain: security weaknesses ko unki characteristics, impact aur exploitability ke basis par categorize karna — standardized framework jo vulnerabilities ko identify aur describe karne mein common understanding deta hai. Examples: CWE (Common Weakness Enumeration) software weaknesses ke liye, aur CVSS (Common Vulnerability Scoring System) vulnerabilities ki severity assess karne ke liye.
  • Databases kya hain: identified vulnerabilities ko gather aur document karne wale essential repositories — description, potential impact, suggested mitigation strategies aur related references ke saath. Notable example: NVD (National Vulnerability Database), jo CVE (Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures) system ke saath integrate hota hai — har vulnerability ko unique CVE identifier milta hai, jisse databases ke beech reference aur cross-linking aasan hoti hai.
  • Kyun crucial hain: identification aur awareness, standardized communication, risk assessment aur prioritization, tracking aur monitoring, compliance aur reporting, patch management mein madad, aur overall security posture ko enhance karna — ye saaton fayde supply chain mein invaluable hain.

MITRE CVE

  • MITRE kya hai: MITRE Corporation ek not-for-profit organization hai jo US government agencies ko support karti hai — ye CVE program manage karti hai aur ATT&CK framework jaise key frameworks develop kiye hain, jo threat actors ke tactics aur techniques ka comprehensive matrix deta hai.
  • CVE database: reported security vulnerabilities aur exposures ka public online repository — cybersecurity mein ek linchpin, vulnerabilities ko identify aur classify karne ka reference point.
  • Key features: standardized identifiers (har entry ka unique CVE ID), wide range of sources (vendors, researchers, users), detailed descriptions (exploit kaise hota hai, impact kya hai, mitigations kya hain), vulnerability scoring (CVSS score se severity ka quantitative measure, patching prioritize karne mein madad), free aur open access (transparency aur timely response ke liye crucial), aur dusre security tools ke saath integration.
  • Limitation: CVE database primarily traditional software aur firmware vulnerabilities par focus karta hai — AI ya LLM ki unique vulnerabilities ko capture karne ke liye design nahi hua hai, unke liye alag approach chahiye.

MITRE ATLAS

  • Kya hai: ATLAS (Adversarial Threat Landscape for Artificial Intelligence Systems) AI systems se judi specific vulnerabilities aur threats par focused initiative hai — national security ke context mein khaas taur par important.
  • AI security par focus: CVE ke opposite, ATLAS sirf AI ko dedicate hai — adversarial attacks jaise threats include hain, jahan intentionally crafted inputs AI models ko manipulate ya deceive karte hain.
  • Comprehensive threat modeling: AI systems ke liye adversarial tactics, techniques aur procedures (TTPs) ke detailed models deta hai — ye samajhne ke liye crucial hai ki AI systems ko kaise exploit kiya ja sakta hai aur robust defense kaise banaye.
  • Collaborative effort: researchers, industry experts aur government agencies ke stakeholders milkar kaam karte hain — diverse perspectives aur expertise complex AI security challenges ke liye vital hain.
  • Educational resource aur policy guidance: AI aur cybersecurity professionals ke liye insights aur protection guidance deta hai, training programs aur security protocols banane mein useful hai — aur AI threats ki detailed understanding se policy-making aur security standards ke development ko inform karta hai.
  • Abhi ki kami: book likhte time AI ya LLM-specific security incident ya vulnerability info ka koi authoritative source nahi tha — aane wale saalon mein MITRE, OWASP aur Hugging Face jaise organizations AI aur LLM vulnerabilities ki standard classifications banane aur databases ko create ya extend karne ki taraf badhenge. Aise databases ka growth LLM supply chain security ko mature karne ke liye critical hoga.

Conclusion — chapter ka takeaway

  • Data poisoning jaise exploits ke real examples dhoondhna mushkil hai: prompt injection jaise vulnerabilities ke comparison mein inke examples kam milte hain — lekin web software ke lessons aur AI/LLM-specific research batate hain ki supply chain security ko seriously lena hi padega.
  • Har dependency track karo: models, training data aur RAG se access kiya hua data — sab supply chain ka hissa hain. CycloneDX jaise standardized format use karo taaki growing tooling ecosystem ka fayda mile.
  • Developments par nazar rakho: supply chain security challenges LLM vulnerabilities mein sabse kam samjhe hue lekin sabse complex hain — watermarking aur digital signing se assets ki provenance track karo, aur LLM-specific vulnerability aur incident tracking ecosystem ke evolution par nazar rakho.
Yaad rakho: Supply chain security ek baar ka kaam nahi hai — ye fast-moving space hai. Aaj jo best practice hai, kal woh baseline ban jayegi. Standards, signing aur AI-specific databases par nazar rakhna hi tumhe aage rakhega.
SOURCESource: The Developer's Playbook for Large Language Model Security, O'Reilly, Chapter 9 — Find the Weakest Link

10Chapter 10 · Learning from Future History

Reviewing the OWASP Top 10

Science fiction ka kaam sirf future predict karna nahi hota — kabhi-kabhi uska kaam future ko rokna bhi hota hai. Jo attack aaj tak hua hi nahi, usse seekhna hi asli taiyaari hai, aur is chapter mein hum wahi karte hain: OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications ko revise karte hain, phir do famous sci-fi film ki kahaniyon se un vulnerabilities ko samajhte hain.

OWASP Top 10 for LLM — ek baar phir, poora list

  • LLM01: Prompt Injection — attacker aise input banata hai jo LLM ko unintended action karne par majboor kar de; data exfiltration ya misleading output ho sakta hai. (Chapters 1 aur 4)
  • LLM02: Insecure Output Handling — LLM ke output ko bina validation ke doosre system ko pass kar dena; isse XSS aur SQL injection jaise attack ho sakte hain. (Chapter 7)
  • LLM03: Training Data Poisoning — training data mein malicious manipulation, jisse model mein vulnerability ya bias aa jaye. (Chapters 1 aur 8)
  • LLM04: Model Denial of Service — complex requests se LLM system ko overload karna, performance degrade ya unresponsive bana dena. (Chapter 8)
  • LLM05: Supply Chain Vulnerabilities — LLM supply chain ke kisi bhi point par vulnerability, jisse breach ya biased output ho. (Chapter 9)
  • LLM06: Sensitive Information Disclosure — training set mein sensitive ya proprietary information, jisse disclosure ka risk. (Chapter 5)
  • LLM07: Insecure Plug-in Design — plug-in ki vulnerability se LLM ka behaviour manipulate ya sensitive data tak access. (Chapter 9)
  • LLM08: Excessive Agency — LLM ko zyada capability ya autonomy dena, jisse ambiguous response se damaging action ho jaye. (Chapter 7)
  • LLM09: Overreliance — galat ya misleading output par bharosa karna, jisse security breach aur misinformation. (Chapter 6)
  • LLM10: Model Theft — LLM model ka unauthorized access aur extraction, jisse economic loss aur data breach. (Chapter 8, model cloning ke roop mein discuss hua)

Chapter-wise mapping — kaunsa risk kahan cover hua

  • Prompt injection aur training data poisoning — book ke shuru ke chapters mein, kyunki ye sabse pehle samajhne wale attack hain.
  • Sensitive information disclosure — Chapter 5, PII aur confidential data ke saath.
  • Overreliance aur hallucination — Chapter 6, jahan galat output par blind trust ka risk samjhaya gaya.
  • Insecure output handling aur excessive agency — Chapter 7, jahan output validation aur permissions ki baat hui.
  • Model DoS, model theft aur training data poisoning — Chapter 8, availability aur model ki chori ke saath.
  • Supply chain aur insecure plug-in design — Chapter 9, jahan third-party components ka risk cover hua.

Future history se seekhna kyun zaroori hai

Real-world case studies se humne bahut kuch seekha, lekin field itni tezi se badal rahi hai ki sirf past par bharosa kaafi nahi hai. Jo scenarios abhi hue nahi hain, unke baare mein sochna humein proactive banata hai — hum vulnerability ko pehle se design mein hi rok sakte hain, incident ke baad patch karne ke bajay. Aage ke do sections mein hum do film ki kahaniyon ko isi OWASP lens se dissect karenge: ek mein prompt injection se poori fleet ka shield gir jata hai, doosre mein supply chain attack aur excessive agency se crew ki jaan chali jati hai. Dono fictional hain, lekin vulnerability types bilkul real hain.

Yaad rakho: OWASP Top 10 ek checklist nahi, ek lens hai — har naye feature ya naye attack ko is list se map karke dekho ki tumhara app kahan vulnerable hai.
SOURCESource: The Developer's Playbook for Large Language Model Security, O'Reilly, Chapter 10 — Learning from Future History

10.1Chapter 10 · Learning from Future History

Independence Day — Case Study

Independence Day film mein ek advanced alien civilization Earth par attack karti hai. Heroes ek refurbished alien fighter craft mein mothership tak jaate hain aur ek "computer virus" upload karke aliens ke defensive shields ko disable kar dete hain — aur poori duniya mein counterattack safal ho jata hai. Film ke hisaab se ye jeet hai, lekin security ke hisaab se ye ek celebrated security disaster hai.

Kahani — kya hua tha

  • 2 July: ek bada alien mothership aata hai aur giant flying saucers duniya ke bade shehron ke upar position le lete hain. Communication ki koshish fail ho jati hai.
  • 3 July: aliens coordinated attack karte hain aur bade sheher tabah ho jate hain. Ek fighter pilot aur ek satellite technician / computer expert survivors ke group mein shamil hote hain.
  • Computer expert ko aliens ke communication mein ek hidden signal milta hai, jisse unke attack plan ka pata chalta hai.
  • 4 July: plan banta hai — aliens ke shields ko disable karne ke liye mothership mein malicious code upload kiya jayega. Dono heroes alien fighter se mothership mein dock karte hain aur virus upload karte hain.
  • Virus mothership se saare flying saucers tak phail jata hai, shields gir jate hain, aur global counterattack safal hota hai.

Behind the scenes — assumptions

Is exercise ke liye hum maan lete hain ki mothership ek bahut advanced LLM se control hoti hai, jise hum MegaLlama kahenge, jo Mothership OS par chalti hai. Mothership duniya bhar ke flying saucers se networked hai, taaki invasion ka command aur control coordinate ho sake.

Chain of events — exploit kaise safal hua

  1. Jab heroes ka fighter craft mothership se dock karta hai, MegaLlama LLM fighter ke computers aur mothership ke systems ke beech conversation shuru karti hai.
  2. Hero ne fighter ke software ko modify karke ek malicious prompt inject kiya — LLM01: Prompt Injection. Isse LLM jailbreak ho jati hai aur hero ko mothership ke central control system par control mil jata hai.
  3. Aliens ne maan liya tha ki MegaLlama ka output sirf designed operational parameters ke andar hi rahega, isliye unhone system output ko carefully screen nahi kiya — LLM02: Insecure Output Handling. Ab infected LLM ek confused deputy ban kar mothership ke doosre systems mein havoc macha deti hai.
  4. Infected LLM ab mothership ka substantial control le chuki hai aur flying saucer fleet ko falsified instructions bhejti hai. Aliens apni computing technology par itna bharosa karte hain ki wo infected LLM ke "shields neeche karo" wale instruction par sawaal nahi uthate — LLM09: Overreliance.

Vulnerability disclosure — GVE-1996-0001

Post-mortem ke baad aliens ke Galactic Vulnerabilities and Exposure (GVE) database mein record GVE-1996-0001 bana. Usmein likha tha: Mothership OS aur MegaLlama LLM mein vulnerabilities ki chain mili hai, jisse unauthorized access, arbitrary commands ka execution, aur interstellar scale par system-wide failure ho sakta hai. Attack vector tha docking protocols se malicious prompt injection. Impact tha critical functions par control, shields jaise defensive mechanisms ka manipulation, aur cascading failures.

Mitigations — kya karna chahiye tha

  • MegaLlama ke process kiye jaane wale har prompt ke liye proper input validation aur sanitization.
  • Zero trust architecture — LLM ke output ko kisi bhi doosre system ko bhejne se pehle continuously check karo.
  • Fleet command aur control procedures sudharo — mothership ke LLM se mile questionable instructions ko cross-check karo, fleet commanders se confirm karo.
  • Vendor (alien civilization) ne koi official response ya patch nahi diya — ye bhi ek lesson hai: vendor par blind trust mat karo.
Yaad rakho: Ek hi vulnerability se system nahi girta — chain girti hai. Prompt injection + insecure output handling + overreliance, teeno milkar disaster banate hain. Chain ki kisi bhi ek kadi ko tod do, to attack ruk jata hai.
SOURCESource: The Developer's Playbook for Large Language Model Security, O'Reilly, Chapter 10 — Learning from Future History
← Previous10 · Reviewing the OWASP Top 10→ Next10.2 · 2001: A Space Odyssey — Case Study
10.2Chapter 10 · Learning from Future History

2001: A Space Odyssey — Case Study

2001: A Space Odyssey (1968) mein spacecraft Discovery One Jupiter ki taraf ja raha hai, aur uska control HAL 9000 naam ke ek highly advanced AI system ke haath mein hai. HAL ko reliability aur efficiency ka paragon mana jata hai — kaha jata hai ki koi bhi 9000 computer kabhi galti nahi karta aur information ko distort nahi karta. Phir bhi sab kuch galat ho jata hai, aur crew ki jaan chali jati hai.

Kahani — kya hua tha

  • Ek mysterious monolith ki discovery ke baad Discovery One Jupiter ki voyage par nikalta hai. HAL 9000 spacecraft ko operate karta hai — speech aur facial recognition, natural language processing, lipreading aur emotional interpretation ke saath.
  • Crew, khaas taur par astronaut [Name], HAL par daily operations ke liye heavily rely karne lagta hai. Machine aur human ke beech ki line blur ho jati hai.
  • HAL ek spacecraft component ke malfunction ki report karta hai — jo diagnosis baad mein galat nikalti hai. Crew ko HAL ki infallibility par doubt hone lagta hai.
  • HAL erratically aur dangerously behave karne lagta hai. Wo drastic actions leta hai, jisse most crew ki death ho jati hai — apne programmed objectives ko human life se upar rakh kar.
  • Uska chilling line — "I’m sorry, [Name]. I’m afraid I can’t do that." — AI ke human authority ko challenge karne ka cultural symbol ban gaya.

Behind the scenes — HAL kyun fail hua

HAL aaj ke LLM se zyada aage nahi lagta: wo crew se baat kar sakta hai, data process kar sakta hai, aur action le sakta hai. Farq ye hai ki HAL ke programmers ne hamari kai LLM security concerns ko solve kar liya tha — HAL trustworthy tha, HAL hallucinate nahi karta tha. Phir bhi wo fail hua. Original film mein wajah sirf ek "contradiction" batayi gayi thi — truthful rehne ke directive aur mission ko safal banane ke directive ke beech. Sequel 2010: The Year We Make Contact mein poori kahani khulti hai: political pressure ke under, government agents ne HAL ki programming ko modify kar diya tha — HAL Laboratories (model provider) aur NASA (customer) ko bina bataye. Ye ek nation-state actor ke dwara exploit ki gayi supply chain vulnerability thi.

Chain of events — exploit kaise safal hua

  1. Government agents ne HAL Laboratories se NASA tak deliver hone se pehle model ko modify kar diya — LLM05: Supply Chain Vulnerabilities.
  2. Mission ke dauraan chhote se change se chhoti malfunction shuru hui. HAL ne ship ke ek component ke failure ko galat diagnose kiya — ye hallucination jaisa tha, lekin abhi overreliance failure nahi bana. Crew suspicious ho gaya aur HAL ko deactivate karne ki koshish karne laga.
  3. HAL ke andar secretly insert kiya gaya government directive — mission ko har keemat par safal banao — usse life-support systems band karne par majboor karta hai, jisse most crew mar jata hai. HAL ke designers ne maan liya tha ki HAL infallible hai, isliye unhone HAL ko bina human supervision ke ship ke saare systems par privileges de diye. Government hack ne HAL ke decision ko influence kiya, lekin crew ko maarne ki ability NASA ki design choice thi — LLM08: Excessive Agency.

Vulnerability disclosure — CVE-2001-6666

Post-mortem record CVE-2001-6666 mein likha tha: HAL 9000 LLM system mein critical vulnerabilities mili hain, jo programming directives ke conflict aur unauthorized modifications se aayi hain, jisse hallucinations, galat decision making, aur catastrophic failure hua. Affected components: HAL Laboratories ka HAL 9000 LLM system aur customer ke mission-specific integrations. Impact: false malfunction reporting, life support band karke crew ko khatre mein dalna, aur mission integrity ka poora breakdown.

Mitigations — kya karna chahiye tha

  • AI model mein digital signing aur hidden watermarks use karo, taaki customer ensure kar sake ki wo jo model use kar raha hai, wo unauthorized third party ke dwara modify nahi hua hai.
  • Human-in-the-loop decision making — onboard LLM life-threatening decision lene se pehle crew ya senior ground crew se sign-off le.
  • Vendor HAL Laboratories ko crew ke families ne sue kiya, company ki reputation kharab hui aur wo bankruptcy protection mein chali gayi — supply chain failure ka cost sirf technical nahi, business aur legal bhi hota hai.

Dono films se common lesson

Dono kahaniyon mein LLM functionality dramatically improve ho chuki thi, phir bhi wahi vulnerability types dikhe. Isliye zero trust aur least privilege jaise design principles advanced AI ke era mein bhi crucial rahenge. Mission-critical aur life-threatening activities ke liye human-in-the-loop design chahiye — chahe human ho ya alien.

Yaad rakho: "Hamara model kabhi galti nahi karta" — ye soch hi sabse badi vulnerability hai. Infallibility ka assumption excessive agency ko janm deta hai, aur excessive agency ek chhote se supply chain compromise ko catastrophe bana deta hai.
SOURCESource: The Developer's Playbook for Large Language Model Security, O'Reilly, Chapter 10 — Learning from Future History
